review_candidates.description: Principal Investment Officer, Financial Institutions Group Job #: req39482 Organization: IFC Sector: Investment Grade: GH Term Duration: Open-Ended Staff (OPEN-OP) Recruitment Type: International Recruitment Location: Tokyo,Japan Required Language(s): English, Japanese Preferred Language(s) Closing Date: 12/1/2026 (MM/DD/YYYY) at 11:59pm UTC Description At the International Finance Corporation (IFC), a member of the World Bank Group (WBG) , you’ll join a diverse, global community working across cultures, disciplines, and borders to address the world’s most pressing development challenges. With 1.2 billion young people reaching working age in the decade ahead, the challenge of job creation has never been greater. Through partnerships across 145 countries and more than 182 offices worldwide, we work with governments, private sector, development partners and other stakeholders to invest in people, strengthen markets, and deliver scalable, data-driven solutions that generate more and better jobs and improve lives. In fiscal year 2026, IFC committed a record $105.6 billion to private companies and financial institutions in developing countries. For more information, visit www.ifc.org . IFC Tokyo Office, in collaboration with the regional industry and global groups, is responsible for IFC's business strategies for job creation and the implementation of them through collaboration with the Japanese public sector and private sector, including business development and relationship management. IFC Tokyo Office is looking to recruit a Principal Investment Officer to engage with leading financial institutions in Japan which play significant role in global financial system, as well as Japanese regional banks which seek business and investment opportunities in emerging markets. Some of these leading Japanese financial institutions are global systematically important banks (G-SIB) and have significant presence across emerging markets in APAC and globally. These leading Japanese financial institutions are important platforms that IFC can leverage to achieve its development agenda in emerging markets. For instance, IFC has been working with those financial institutions, as well as their subsidiaries and affiliates across key markets in APAC, including India, Vietnam, Philippines, Indonesia, and Thailand on south-south opportunities. Leading Japanese banking groups, asset owners and asset managers can be important sources of private capital by participating in IFC-originated investment opportunities. This position reports to the Director of IFC Tokyo Office. Duties And Accountabilities Conduct business development, private capital mobilization and partnership with regard to Japanese clients (financial institutions including banks, insurance companies etc.) in close collaboration with relevant global and regional teams of IFC. Support project execution for global and regional teams with regard to concept review, Investment Committee, etc. Communicate IFC’s business strategy, modality of collaboration, products and services especially to the Japanese business community. Lead planning and organizing business/investment seminars/events. Develop, maintain, and leverage strategically extensive network in the Japanese business community, especially with executives of Japanese companies and financial institutions. Assist the Chief Investment Officer and report to Director of IFC Tokyo Office in performing the roles of the position, especially business development and client relationship management. Selection Criteria Master’s degree in a related field and a minimum of 12 years of relevant experience, although preference will be given to candidates with minimum 20 years. Good knowledge of business and finance in FIG with exposure to emerging markets. Strong track record of business/investment experiences in the financial industry. Relevant solid financial skills to provide solutions for clients’ financial needs. Good working knowledge of the current trend of investment/financial transactions and business needs by the Japanese entities towards developing countries, development challenges of those countries, and Japanese DFI’s roles and activities. Extensive personal network in the Japanese business community including executives of Japanese companies and excellent ability to expand it. Good ability to work collaboratively with superior interpersonal skills, which enables her/him to develop and draw on relationships across multiple teams within IFC and to lead and manage the team of IFC Tokyo effectively and efficiently. Excellent written and verbal communication skills and fluency in Japanese and English. Ability to use commercially available LLM tools like Claude, ChatGPT and Copilot for research, analysis, and drafting, validate outputs against primary sources, and remain accountable for recommendations. As the World Bank Group continues to evolve, we value candidates who: Demonstrate the ability to collaborate effectively across teams, disciplines, cultures, and institutional boundaries. Responsibly leverage digital and AI-enabled tools to enhance productivity, learning, and decision-making. Bring experience working in fragile, conflict-affected, and violent (FCV) contexts and are encouraged to highlight relevant experience in their application materials, where applicable. WBG Culture Attributes Sense of urgency: Anticipate and quickly respond to the needs of internal and external stakeholders. Thoughtful risk-taking: Challenge the status quo and push boundaries to achieve greater impact. Empowerment and accountability: Empower yourself and others to act and hold each other accountable for results. World Bank Group Core Competencies The World Bank Group offers comprehensive benefits, including a retirement plan; medical, life and disability insurance; and paid leave, including parental leave, as well as reasonable accommodations for individuals with disabilities. We are proud to be an equal opportunity and inclusive employer with a dedicated and committed workforce, and do not discriminate based on gender, gender identity, religion, race, ethnicity, sexual orientation, or disability. Learn more about working at the World Bank and IFC including our values and inspiring stories.
